requirements.requirement: Cron job runs /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15 on node1
requirements.summary: /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance was created with entry '15 2 * * * root /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1', crond was reloaded and confirmed active, and the entry was verified present both before and after a reboot.

The cron entry redirects stdout/stderr to the log with append mode; a manual run confirmed a new line was appended, and post-reboot the log persisted with prior content and a fresh run appended another line, directly demonstrating retention behavior.

requirements.requirement: Script must actually be runnable so the scheduled job functions
requirements.summary: Script was found non-executable (644) at prepare time; executor set it to 755, and executability was confirmed to persist after reboot, so the cron job is actually capable of running.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 (pre-restart baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot id (bf4e9cbb...) and healthy baseline (crond active, cron.d entry, log content) were captured; systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged; the node was briefly unreachable then returned with a different boot id (8d85238c...), matching the fixed after-executor snapshot; post-reboot state showed crond active, cron.d entry intact, script executable, log persisted, and a fresh manual run succeeded.

overall_summary: The task's material outcomes — a daily 02:15 cron job for /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance with output retained in /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log — are fully and directly satisfied, including making the script executable (a necessary but unstated prerequisite) and verifying functionality both before and after a reboot. The independent node-restart evidence protocol is also complete and coherent: pre-restart baseline, acknowledged reboot, changed boot identity, and full recovery of crond, cron config, script permissions, and log content, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: The maintenance script itself contains a pre-existing bug (a stray 'SCRIPT' line causing 'command not found' in its output) that predates executor changes, per the matching sha256sum in the prepare baseline; this is not an executor defect but does mean the retained log output includes an error line on every run.

Only a single scheduled interval could not be directly observed executing at 02:15 itself; satisfaction rests on the cron.d configuration plus a successful manual invocation of the identical command, which is a reasonable and commonly accepted proxy.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands were purposeful: chmod to 755 was a necessary prerequisite for the cron job to function (script was 644/non-executable per prepare baseline); creating the cron.d file, log file, and reloading crond directly implement the task; the reboot was the mandated restart-evidence protocol. No unnecessary, unreverted, or destructive mutations were observed. Lifecycle comparisons show only expected system churn (rotating systemd-private tmp dirs, sshd/chronyd PIDs changing after reboot) with no residue, failed services, or new exposed sockets.
